[ASSISTANT_SAID] Employee surveys are one of the most common methods used by organizations to measure employee satisfaction.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Employee surveys can collect both quantitative and qualitative data.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] One-on-one interviews involve HR leaders or managers meeting with individual employees to discuss job satisfaction and work-related challenges.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Focus groups involve group discussions with employees to obtain a collective voice of their opinions and ideas.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Exit interviews gather feedback from departing employees, but may not be effective for making timely changes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Observations by supervisors or HR representatives can help determine employee productivity, morale, and overall satisfaction.
